Fake COVID-19 Certificates Sold By Criminals

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In South Africa, travellers must show a negative COVID-19 test certificate for travel and work purposes, but the production and sale of fake tests certificates suggest the results aren't all authentic

Unique Selling Point:
Allegations of Covid-19 testing fraud have been cropping up around the world and our country is not immune to this type of crime. How easy it is to purchase a fake COVID-19 certificate? Carte Blanche investigates.

Summary:
Illicit sales of fake negative COVID-19 test results are becoming more widespread as criminals look to profit from travel restrictions imposed during the pandemic. Based on research, ANYONE can purchase a negative coronavirus test for R400. We investigated one such place in Kempton Park. A man, who calls himself Cyber Craft, has been selling these fake documents after South Africa and other countries oblige travelers to present this essential document.

Further information:
The fake one that we purchased has a letterhead from AMPATH Laboratories ((Please see attached picture)), as well as a fresh stamp from a so-called Dr E Peers, who doesn't even exist. Cyber Craft says his customers are not only desperate travellers but people who are eager to go back to work. These black market certificates not only threaten the health of other travellers, they are also undermining the aviation sector’s efforts to limit the spread of the disease. For this story we will speak to Cyber Craft who is selling the fake certificates, Martha Thunji who admits to purchasing one which helped secure her flight to Zimbabwe and an aviation expert. Martha says she did it because real COVID-19 test are very expensive and not accessible to people with real money challenges. She also added that many of her friends who wished to travel home didn’t because their tests came back positive. This is despite them feeling “well”. This tells us that many travellers who are asymptomatic may travel with a fake certificate and can possibly affect others.

Press Release:


False Negative – the COVID-19 Black Market
As travel restrictions remain in place globally for anyone who tests COVID-19 positive, a black market in fake negative test results is flourishing as criminals seek to profit from people’s desperation to resume normal life amid the pandemic. Carte Blanche investigates a local supplier of fraudulent certificates and examines the consequences for travellers as fake certificates are accepted at various ports of entry - potentially exposing fellow passengers to the danger of contracting the virus.

Script:


SCRIPT - FAKE COVID-19 CERTIFICATES

VO - COVID-19 has significantly changed the way that we travel and most countries worldwide demand proof of a negative COVID-19 test result, before letting you in. Such restrictions have given rise to fraudulent fit-to-travel certificates sold on the black market.

LINK 1 [MacFarlane Moleli] - At first glance, this negative COVID-19 test certificate would look real enough to most eyes. It has the passenger’s personal information and also bears an official logo of one of the most trusted laboratories in South Africa. But this document is actually a fraud.

VO - An increasing number of people are buying these certificates prior to travelling, potentially exposing fellow passengers to the danger of contracting the virus.

VO - These fake test results have become a growing concern globally and authorities in South Africa are also beginning to grapple with it, says aviation expert Guy Leitch.

SOUND [Guy Leitch] 05:18 This goes back to the credibility of the South African system of checks and balances. It will simply make it that much more difficult for South Africans to travel later on if we can’t get on top of it.

VO - Producing or even attempting to buy a forged certificate is a crime but this is not stopping people like this 35 year old traveller. We call him Ray.

SOUND [RAY] 06:06 - Well it was a gamble … I knew exactly what I was doing and I know it was a 50/50 chance I could get caught and I suppose the reasons why I was traveling were quite important at that time.

In December last year, Ray travelled from South Africa to Zimbabwe using an authentic COVID-19 certificate which cost him a total of R1 500. This included a doctor’s consultation fee of R400. But an unexpected emergency involving his son compelled him to turn to the black market to purchase a fake COVID-19 test document for his trip back into South Africa.

ADD MAC QUESTION - 0:59 WHAT COMPELLED YOU THEN TO GO LOOK FOR A FAKE COVID-19 CERTIFICATE?

SOUND [RAY] 15:22 ... While I was in ZIm I left him in the care of my cousin and they went out with my cousin's child and he nearly drowned and was rushed to the hospital.

VO - Ray had to change his flight bookings and rushed to a private laboratory in Zimbabwe for a covid-19 test, only to discover that he could not afford one.

SOUND - [RAY] 21:58 the security guard heard me asking all these questions. While I was walking he came to me and said he can help me for half the price. I asked him what he was talking about and he said he can get me a proper test results in two hours if you give us $30.
VO - That’s about R450,00 which helped him secure an early trip back to South Africa.
23:52- I got the test results certificate from him and paid him and I was out and ready to travel later that evening.
LINK - [MacFarlane Moleli] … So what measures should be implemented to ensure the authenticity of a COVID-19 test certificate before travelling?
VO - With various airports stepping up COVID-19 checks and procedures prior to departure, staff are increasingly struggling to cope with the added pressure of policing the veracity of pre-flight COVID-19 test results. Airport staff are sometimes unable to tell whether additional COVID-19 paperwork, presented by travellers, is genuine.
VO - Ray’s last minute forged document gave him no problems at the Robert Mugabe International Airport where he departed.
SOUND - [RAY] 24:20 ... as I was going through to immigration somebody stopped me and said can I please see your covid results. 24:43- There I was thinking oh okay this is it now. He looked at it for a few seconds and he let me go.
VO - He was also successful in fooling security staff when he arrived at the O.R Tambo International Airport, he says.
Leitch says such crime could be avoided if South Africa implements an integrated authentication system that is on par with the rest of the world.
10:27 It requires an enormous amount of integration with many other different sources, for instance, with the laboratories on one hand, ID sources with databases. Its incredibly complex to create a digital process like this
VO - Personal travel is not the only reason why people buy fake certificates. This 38 year old cross-border truck driver with twelve years experience under his belt, buys HIS for work purposes. We call him Sipho.
SOUND - [SIPHO] 1:31- For the company I work for, I travel between South Africa and Zim and sometimes go to Zambia too but because of covid we have lost many clients so now it’s mainly South Africa to Zim.
VO - Despite crossing borders regularly, Sipho has NEVER tested for COVID-19.
VO - He blames this on his employer who he says is reluctant to pay for his tests.
SOUND - [SIPHO] 11:00- Companies don’t assist you with getting tested for covid. All they want is you to do it on your own and continue working.
VO - And so he goes for the cheapest option - a fake fit-to-travel test certificate that will not break the bank.
SOUND - [SIPHO] 16:05 - Before the certificate was R200 or R150 but right now you can easily get one for R100 because of competition.
MAC : When you say competition, it means you can get it anywhere?
Sipho: Yes!
VO - Home Affairs Minister Aaron Motsoaledi says cross border drivers like Sipho could be arrested and charged with fraud, in addition to a five-year ban from entering South Africa.
SOUND - [Aaron Motsoaledi] 1804 we caught a large number of people and detained them. 18:23 You could easily suspect when a certificate is fake and the people of port health are trained to recognise certificates that are illegitimate and authentic. You just call the lab and find that they don’t exist.
VO - Sipho prefers to get his fake certificates printed at Internet Cafes in Kempton Park, a few kilometers away from his workplace.
SOUND - [SIPHO] 12:32 You just get to these cafes and you speak to a guy and he gives you what you want.12:33 You give the guy your name and all your details then he prints it out for you.

LINK [MacFarlane Moleli] As long as travel restrictions remain in place due to the pandemic, it is highly likely that the production and sale of fake certificates will prevail.
VO - With the help of an operative Carte Blanche went undercover at one such establishment at Voortreker road, in Kempton Park….and found a man who was eager to help.
00:56 Researcher : It’s valid for how long?
Fraudster: If it's for drivers it's one month. If it's for a normal person it's 15 days.
Researcher: For flying out?
01;07 For two days, yeah.
VO - Moments later, a fake COVID-19 certificate is printed out for R200.

VO - The fraudulent certificate our operative received has a logo from AMPATH, as well as a contact number of the alleged patient.

LINK 2 [MacFarlane Moleli] So we found a number on this fake COVID-19 certificate, we don’t know who it belongs to and this person might not also be aware that their number is being used for fraudulent means. So let’s give it a call and see who we get on the other side.

PHONE ; “you have reached the voicemail service of...goodbye”

Mac: No surprises there, fraudulent certificate - obviously a fraudulent number.




VO - Upon inspection, AMPATH CEO Dr Forder identified some of the red flags that suggest the document is fake.

SOUND - [Dr Mick Forder]

NATSOUND 02:19 We condemn it in the strongest possible terms…3:38 it's become quite prevalent out there and that’s of major concern

SOUND [Dr Mick Forder] 23:44 – 25:00 Dr: So the fraudulent document at this stage the one you sent us anyway contains an old logo in the right hand top corner we have changed that logo now to reflect the new Ampath logo which is in the top left hand corner.

SOUND [Dr Mick Forder] 24:17And the second thing is that just beneath what’s called the referring doctor is a url address and next to that is a verification code. Now that is only printed from our database so the fraudulent report does not have that url address or that verification code on it because they can’t copy that

VO - Dr Forder says that AMPATH has a centralised database App that allows effortless cross-checking but not everyone has embraced it.

SOUND UP [MAC }How easily accessible then is your system?

13:30 – 14:43
Dr: Macfallen from the patient point of view the easiest and best way is through patient app that anybody can download, and it can be verified. Once you have downloaded the report from the app, that cannot be changed. At this stage there are a lot of people including the boarder authorities who won’t accept the App as a report, they want a printed document and once you print a document it then becomes easy to change and fraudulently copy it. Employers and possibly border authorities need to consider whether they will accept an electronic report.
VO - After we were certain of the business’ clandestine operations, we went back on another day to confront the owner.

QUE - CONFRONTATION

00;35 [MAC] WHY ARE YOU GUYS MAKING COVID-19 CERTIFICATES?
We have you on camera selling fake covid-19 certificates. Do you know that it's illegal?

**No one answers***

01;18 [MAC] But why did you start doing it? You want to make quick money?

Fraudster: No that’s not true

MAC 02:00 How long have you been doing it for?

Fraudster Last week.
MAC 02:23 In december you were saying you were busy, yes in, December we have it.
Owner: By december?
MAC: yes, on camera we have it
What you are doing is illegal. Stop doing it! You are putting people’s lives in danger and people can die because of this.
LINK- [MacFarlane Moleli] - So fortunately when we got here, we found the owner and he claims that he didn't know that this activity was happening here at the shop, but he has spoken to his brother, who he says he is the one who was doing it and hopefully they have promised to stop what they are doing.
VO - It's impossible to quantify how much test result fraud is already taking place. But such establishments show the extent to which criminals are taking advantage of the system.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In South Africa, travellers must show a negative COVID-19 test certificate for travel and work purposes, but the production and sale of fake tests certificates suggest the results aren't all authentic
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Allegations of Covid-19 testing fraud have been cropping up around the world and our country is not immune to this type of crime. How easy it is to purchase a fake COVID-19 certificate? Carte Blanche investigates.
metadata.Summary: Illicit sales of fake negative COVID-19 test results are becoming more widespread as criminals look to profit from travel restrictions imposed during the pandemic. Based on research, ANYONE can purchase a negative coronavirus test for R400. We investigated one such place in Kempton Park. A man, who calls himself Cyber Craft, has been selling these fake documents after South Africa and other countries oblige travelers to present this essential document.
metadata.Further information: The fake one that we purchased has a letterhead from AMPATH Laboratories ((Please see attached picture)), as well as a fresh stamp from a so-called Dr E Peers, who doesn't even exist. Cyber Craft says his customers are not only desperate travellers but people who are eager to go back to work. These black market certificates not only threaten the health of other travellers, they are also undermining the aviation sector’s efforts to limit the spread of the disease. For this story we will speak to Cyber Craft who is selling the fake certificates, Martha Thunji who admits to purchasing one which helped secure her flight to Zimbabwe and an aviation expert. Martha says she did it because real COVID-19 test are very expensive and not accessible to people with real money challenges. She also added that many of her friends who wished to travel home didn’t because their tests came back positive. This is despite them feeling “well”. This tells us that many travellers who are asymptomatic may travel with a fake certificate and can possibly affect others.
